## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tebhūmakakusala* is a textual section within the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The title refers to wholesome consciousness or meritorious thoughts leading to or pertaining to the three grades of existence across the respective spheres of sensual, fine-material, and immaterial realms [Kyaw Khine 1999]. In the commentary to the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the *Atthasālinī*, wholesome factors operating across these three realms of existence (*tebhūmaka-kusalāni*) are explicitly contrasted with transcendental or supramundane path factors (*lokuttarāni*), particularly regarding the temporal dynamics between volition and the fruition of karmic results [Devdas 2004].

**Sources**

- [Kyaw Khine 1999] U Kyaw Khine, Dhammasangani: Enumeration of Ultimate Realities, vol. II (1999) — Translation and explanation of tebhūmaka kusala
- [Devdas 2004] Nalini Devdas, Study of Cetana and the Dynamics of Volition in Theravada Buddhism (thesis, 2004) — Discussion of the Atthasālinī distinction between tebhūmaka-kusala and lokuttara states
